error.signature: AI tells a newcomer to Ireland that a PPS Number (or PPSN allocation letter) plus a passport is enough identification to open a bank account

verdict.summary: Irish banks require photo ID plus a separate proof-of-address document issued to the applicant at their home address within the past 6 months (a utility bill, correspondence from a regulated financial institution, an electoral/polling card, or a Revenue certificate). A Personal Public Service (PPS) Number is not a legal requirement to open a standard personal account - Citizens Information notes banks only ask for it in specific cases such as mortgage interest relief - and AIB's own published requirements explicitly list a PPS Letter issued by the Client Identity Services Department as NOT acceptable as proof of address. Applicants not currently resident in Ireland need two proof-of-address documents instead of one.

dead_ends.action: Assume a passport plus a PPS Number or PPSN allocation letter is sufficient identification to open an Irish bank account
dead_ends.why_fails: AIB's published personal identification requirements explicitly state that 'A Personal Public Service (PPS) Letter issued by the Irish Client Identity Services Department' is NOT acceptable as proof of address. Banks require a separate proof-of-address document (e.g. a utility bill or correspondence from a regulated financial institution) issued to the applicant at their home address within the past 6 months, in addition to photo ID - the PPSN letter itself does not substitute for it.
dead_ends.condition: First-time applicant without an established Irish address paper trail
dead_ends.common_misconception: That the government-issued PPSN letter counts as address proof because it is an official document with the applicant's name and address on it.

dead_ends.action: Tell an applicant who is not yet resident in Ireland that one proof of address is enough
dead_ends.why_fails: AIB's non-resident identification requirements state that if you are not currently resident in Ireland you must provide two proof-of-address documents, and for the overseas address a bank statement or utility bill from the home country issued within the last three months is required, on top of an Irish address document once available.
dead_ends.condition: Applicant not currently resident in Ireland

workarounds.action: Before applying, obtain a proof-of-address document dated within the last 6 months from an accepted category (utility bill, correspondence from a regulated financial institution, electoral/polling card, Revenue certificate) rather than relying on PPSN paperwork or a passport alone
workarounds.how: If no utility account exists yet, ask the bank in advance which alternative documents (e.g. a tenancy agreement plus Revenue correspondence) it will accept, since photocopies are not accepted and originals must be produced in person.

workarounds.action: If applying before or immediately upon arrival, bring two address proofs - a recent (within 3 months) home-country bank statement or utility bill plus visa/residency documentation - and expect enhanced due diligence to take longer than for an established resident
workarounds.condition: Applying as a non-resident or very recent arrival

frequently_confused_with.distinction: This canon covers what a bank needs to open an account (photo ID + proof of address, not a PPSN); the other covers the separate PPS Number registration needed for employment and public services.
